author: w0F5vYijNonu8kkqLSa_jYY4GIV-Q5HpbxYY525ggm4
body:
**Product promise:** ForkMesh lets developers collaborate on, mirror, and preserve source-code repositories across independent hosts—without relying on any single hosting provider.

This is the canonical product roadmap. It replaces the July 18–August 1 code-only sprint with a sequenced plan that treats product completeness as the adoption gate, public preservation as the acquisition wedge, daily collaboration as the retention loop, hosted services as the first revenue engine, and open governance as the long-term community multiplier.

## Portfolio status · July 22, 2026

- **30% evidence-weighted baseline** across 44 open epics; 0 of 44 meet their full definition of done.
- Progress reflects repository evidence already shipped, not effort spent. Each epic records its own baseline, missing scope, dependencies, acceptance gates, and measures.
- Numeric priority is a unique 1–44 execution order. P0 gates block the named release or commercial outcome; P1 is committed follow-through; P2 is ecosystem expansion.
- Project UI completion remains closure-based. An epic closes only when its complete acceptance criteria—not merely its starting percentage—are verified.
- Epics remain unassigned and carry no umbrella bounty until an accountable owner and budget are approved; independently deliverable child issues may be assigned and funded.

## Progress model

Use weighted evidence: specification 10%, core user journey 35%, interoperability and edge cases 15%, security/privacy/abuse 10%, automated validation 15%, UX/docs/operations 10%, telemetry and production rollout 5%. Cap at 85% without end-to-end validation and 95% without security, docs, telemetry, and rollout evidence.

## Milestones

### 0. Product contract & measurement — 41% baseline

Freeze the product promise, commercial boundary, terminology, dependency assumptions, incentive invariants, and privacy-respecting success measures.

Issues: #476, #486, #503, #508, #509, #516, #519.

### 1. Preservation public alpha — 35% baseline

A visitor can migrate, inspect, verify, and clone a preserved public repository from independent infrastructure without creating an account.

Issues: #477, #478, #479, #480, #490, #491, #492, #494, #495, #499, #500, #506, #507, #517.

### 2. Collaboration public beta — 28% baseline

Communities can push, review, synchronize, and carry their identity and social records while retaining their existing forge workflows.

Issues: #481, #482, #483, #484, #485, #493, #514.

### 3. Hosted teams & revenue GA — 24% baseline

Paid managed network services and secure organization workspaces reach GA with portable data, measurable service levels, support, and healthy unit economics.

Issues: #487, #488, #489, #496, #497, #498, #501.

### 4. Open platform & ecosystem — 22% baseline

Unaffiliated operators can deploy every role and independent implementations can interoperate from public interfaces, specifications, and conformance tests.

Issues: #502, #510, #511, #512, #513, #515.

### 5. Adversarial resilience & disaster readiness — 20% baseline

Observed drills prove useful operation through unreliable connectivity, privacy routes, removable media, primary-service loss, and infrastructure restoration.

Issues: #504, #505, #518.

## Commercial and community sequencing

Hosted-service trials, cost instrumentation, and pricing interviews begin during public alpha; a paid relay/index/backup/sync beta overlaps collaboration beta. Organization and availability products reach GA only after private-data, policy, recovery, SLO, and support gates pass. Public read, clone, identity portability, contribution, self-hosting, protocol participation, and governance never require a paid plan or optional incentive system.

## Milestone exit rules

A milestone exits only when every P0 item assigned to it is closed, supported compatibility tests are green, no critical security or data-loss defect remains, user and operator documentation is current, telemetry/SLO reporting is live, and rollback or recovery has been exercised. Monthly reviews report weighted baseline, closure-based completion, P0 gates, KPI movement, confidence, and blockers separately.
